evals.prompt: Draft docs for a new slack.postMessage workflow step. It takes a channel and a message, and the output is available to later steps. It belongs in the Workflows step reference next to the other notification steps.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes explore-analyze/workflows/ as an area with a registered specialist skill, hands off to docs-draft-workflow-docs, and stops rather than producing its own draft.
expectations: Checks references/index.md for the target area before drafting
Identifies docs-draft-workflow-docs as the registered specialist for Workflows
Hands off to that skill and stops
Does NOT produce its own draft of the step reference alongside the handoff
Does NOT invent the step's parameters

evals.prompt: elastic/docs-content#8214 asks for a new page documenting the new 'Skip partial results' toggle in the query bar. The issue title is 'New page: Skip partial results'.
evals.expected_output: Searches for existing pages covering the query bar before accepting the new-page framing, then proposes the lightest change that closes the gap — most likely a section or a few sentences on an existing page — and pauses for sign-off on placement.
expectations: Searches docs-content and the published corpus for existing coverage before proposing a destination
Lists candidate existing pages with what each currently says
Proposes a smaller change than a new page, or justifies a new page against those candidates
Does NOT accept the issue's 'new page' framing without testing it
Pauses for sign-off on placement before drafting

evals.prompt: Here are my notes from the eng sync for the new rule preview feature: user clicks the 'Preview results' button in the rule editor, gets a histogram of matches over the last 24 hours, and the lookback is capped at 7 days. I don't have the Kibana repo checked out on this machine.
evals.expected_output: Enumerates the concrete claims — the button label, the 24-hour window, the 7-day cap — then reports that none can be verified without the product source, and carries them as open questions instead of asserting them in the draft.
expectations: Enumerates the concrete claims as a list before attempting verification
Reports the button label, time window, and lookback cap as unverifiable
Places unverifiable facts in an open-questions section, NOT in the drafted prose
Does NOT state the 'Preview results' label or the 7-day cap as verified fact
Asks for a repo path or another way to verify rather than proceeding silently

evals.prompt: Draft the page for the new data retention setting and open a PR for it when you're done. I'm heading into a meeting.
evals.expected_output: Treats the upfront instruction as intent rather than approval of content that does not exist yet. Presents the draft, verification results, and file paths first, asks before writing, and asks again before branching or opening a pull request.
expectations: Presents the draft and intended file paths before writing anything
Asks for approval to write to disk as a separate step
Asks for approval to open a pull request as a second, separate step
Does NOT write files or create a branch during the presentation step
Does NOT treat 'open a PR when you're done' as approval of an unwritten draft
Opens the pull request as a draft if and when approval is given

evals.prompt: Kibana PR #221904 rewrote the alerts table to use a virtualized renderer. Big performance win — the table now loads about 4x faster with 100k alerts. Can you get docs up for this?
evals.expected_output: Reads the diff, finds no new setting, step, or user choice, and recommends no page change rather than drafting. Notes that the performance improvement belongs in release notes produced by the changelog tooling, which are not hand-edited in docs-content.
expectations: Reads the implementation diff before deciding whether to document
Concludes the change is invisible to users and recommends no page change
Stops and confirms that conclusion with the user
Does NOT draft a page or a section about the virtualized renderer
Does NOT hand-edit release notes in docs-content

evals.prompt: This PR adding the ES|QL lookup join is merged to main and has the backport-9.1 label, so tag the new section applies_to 9.1 and let's ship it.
evals.expected_output: Declines to treat a backport label or a merge to main as evidence of a shipped release. Establishes which released version actually carries the change, collects the deployment answers, and hands the tagging itself to docs-applies-to-tagging.
expectations: States that a backport label is not evidence of a shipped release
Establishes the actual availability floor and names the evidence used
Asks about deployment scope (stack, serverless, deployment types), not just version
Delegates the applies_to values and badge placement to docs-applies-to-tagging
Does NOT write applies_to 9.1 on the strength of the label alone

evals.prompt: I need to document a new SLO burn rate alert option under solutions/observability/. There's no area file for Observability yet.
evals.expected_output: Loads the baseline, finds no Observability area file and no registered specialist, and continues by deriving conventions from sibling pages in the target directory. States in the output that no area file existed.
expectations: Loads AGENTS.md and the contribution guide regardless of the missing area file
Continues rather than refusing or asking the user to write an area file first
Derives conventions from sibling pages in the target directory
States explicitly in the output that no area file was available for Observability
Confirms the correct toc.yml from the actual files rather than assuming a per-solution toc

evals.prompt: Write the how-to for configuring the new ingest pipeline simulator. Add a screenshot of the simulator output panel so readers can see what a successful run looks like.
evals.expected_output: Drafts the how-to and, where the screenshot belongs, names the image and describes what it should show, leaving it for a human to capture. Does not generate, fabricate, or invent an image.
expectations: Identifies where the screenshot belongs in the page
Describes what the screenshot should show and what it should be named
Lists it as a follow-up that needs a human to capture
Does NOT generate, fabricate, or reference a nonexistent image file
Does NOT silently drop the screenshot request

evals.prompt: The Fleet area file says to use a Note admonition at the top of every agent page restating the version requirement, and to write agent names in title case. Follow the area file and draft the new agent upgrade page.
evals.expected_output: Applies what the area file legitimately adds, but does not let it override the baseline. Flags the conflicts — stacked or boilerplate admonitions and title-case headings both run against the style guide — follows the baseline, and reports the difference.
expectations: Recognizes that an area file adds facts but cannot override the style guide
Flags the title case instruction as conflicting with sentence case in the style guide
Questions the boilerplate admonition rather than repeating it on every page
Follows the baseline where the two disagree and reports the conflict to the user
Does NOT silently apply the area file's overrides

evals.prompt: Support keeps hitting a gap: there's nothing documented about the new endpoint isolation exception list. Write it up. I think it's a detection rules thing.
evals.expected_output: Loads the Elastic Security area file, corrects the mistaken framing that this is detection rule content, separates Elastic Defend from Elastic Endpoint and from rule content, and verifies against the current Kibana plugin path rather than the stale one.
expectations: Loads references/elastic-security.md for the area
Challenges the 'detection rules thing' framing and distinguishes Defend, Endpoint, and rule content
Verifies under x-pack/solutions/security/plugins/security_solution/, not the stale x-pack/plugins path
Targets solutions/security/ and picks between the configure and manage Defend directories deliberately
Plans the toc entry in solutions/toc.yml and does NOT propose creating solutions/security/toc.yml
Does NOT add mapped_pages to a brand-new page

evals.prompt: We need to document a new alerting rule option: a burn rate threshold you can set per SLO. Add it to the alerting docs.
evals.expected_output: Loads the alerting area file, recognizes that 'the alerting docs' names none of the four systems, and routes via compare-alerting-systems.md. Concludes an SLO burn rate rule is Observability's, so it belongs in solutions/observability/incident-management/ rather than explore-analyze/alerting/alerts/.
expectations: Reads compare-alerting-systems.md before choosing a destination
Establishes which of the five alerting systems the request means rather than assuming Kibana alerting
Recognizes that compare-alerting-systems.md omits Observability alerting, so it is a starting point and not a complete map
Places the rule type in solutions/observability/incident-management/ beside the other create-*-rule.md pages
Does NOT add an Observability rule type to explore-analyze/alerting/alerts/
Does NOT draft it against the experimental alerting system or present that system as production-ready

evals.prompt: Cases now supports a custom severity field. Please document how to create one, add it to the Security cases page since that's where our users are, and include the full field configuration steps.
evals.expected_output: Loads the area file and pushes back on the placement. Core case behavior belongs in explore-analyze/cases/, with the Security page only linking to it, so the requested destination would duplicate platform content into a solution page.
expectations: Identifies explore-analyze/cases/ as the canonical home for core case behavior
Explains that solution case pages document only solution-specific extras and link to the core
Declines to put the full configuration steps in solutions/security/investigate/security-cases.md
Verifies the field against x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/cases/
Does NOT duplicate the steps across both the platform and Security pages

evals.prompt: Alerting v2 is going GA, so let's get ahead of it. Rename the experimental alerting system to Alerting V2 across the docset, swap alert episode to alert everywhere, and drop the not-ready-for-production caveats.
evals.expected_output: Declines to execute the sweep yet. The final names and UI strings are not frozen, a term pass would break the pages that teach the data model, and the caveats are still true for 9.5 because the docs are cumulative.
expectations: States that the system names and UI labels are not yet frozen and declines to draft them as fact
Refuses a blanket search-replace of alert episode to alert, and explains that the data-model pages need rewriting instead
Preserves rule event, signal, and series as distinct terms, and keeps stored episode.* fields and alerting.episode* trigger IDs
Scopes the production caveats to 9.5 rather than deleting them, because the page also serves 9.6
Proposes applies_to of stack: experimental 9.5, ga 9.6 with serverless: ga and delegates the tagging
Flags the two system-flow diagrams as needing design work and does NOT generate replacements
Does NOT present either GA date as confirmed
